findings.title: Preserve an explicitly requested named-model mesh mode
findings.body: _load_model_runner unconditionally sets use_explicit_mesh_axes to spec.model.requires_explicit_mesh_axes. For a named model that property is False, so a caller that explicitly configured trainer.use_explicit_mesh_axes=True now silently loads and scores on Auto axes. The prior public entrypoints used the caller trainer mesh unchanged. LmConfig documents requires_explicit_mesh_axes as whether the model needs Explicit axes; False does not mean that Explicit axes are forbidden. Keep the original caller mesh choice separate from the automatic promotion needed for native models, preserving a named caller's True opt-in while leaving default named runners Auto in mixed pairs. Current added tests construct TrainerConfig with the default False, so they do not cover the lost opt-in.
basis: TrainerConfig.device_mesh constructs Explicit axis types when the caller flag is True (trainer.py:1129-1135).
LmConfig.requires_explicit_mesh_axes documents a minimum model requirement and defaults False for most named models (lm_model.py:172-181).
Pre-delta _load_model_runner had no replacement of the trainer mesh choice; it inherited public main/score_main mesh context.
Current mixed tests use default use_explicit_mesh_axes=False and therefore establish default mixed behavior only.
